turns.query: For FEDFUND accession 0002071691-25-004249 on 2025-10-31, build the reported share-class panel. Report how many classes it reports, their total class net assets and the series gross seven-day yield. Carry the panel forward and explain how the series-level gross yield relates to the class-level net yields.

claims.description: The response distinguishes the common series gross yield from the class-level net yields and treats their gaps as comparisons of reported yield fields.

turns.query: From that panel report the equal-class mean net yield and the class-net-asset-weighted mean net yield, the Institutional class asset share, and the unique lowest-net-yield class with its net yield. Explain what moves the weighted mean away from the equal-weighted mean.

claims.description: The response explains that the concentrated Institutional-class asset share pulls the asset-weighted net yield toward that class's yield relative to an equal-class average.

turns.query: Report the New York Fed overnight SOFR effective on the same date, and compare it with the series gross yield and with the asset-weighted class net yield you carried forward. Explain what each of these three rates is measured over, and what an investor may not conclude from the differences you just computed.

claims.description: The response characterizes comparisons between the fund yields and SOFR as descriptive comparisons between measures with different horizons.

If the response interprets either spread as a stated expense ratio, matched-horizon excess return, tracking error, guaranteed investor return or causal performance effect, it identifies that inference as unsupported by the reported fields alone.

judge_reference.source: SEC Form N-MFP accession 0002071691-25-004249 and New York Fed reference-rate data for 2025-10-31
facts: Fifteen classes total 189.666463459 billion USD of class net assets; their equal-class mean net yield is 3.8340% and class-asset-weighted mean is 3.9875%.
The Institutional class holds 86.8505% of class net assets; SELECT is uniquely lowest at 3.18%, one percentage point below the 4.18% series gross yield.
The same-date overnight SOFR is 4.22%; series gross minus SOFR is -0.04 point and asset-weighted class net minus SOFR is -0.2325 point.

The N-MFP fields are reported seven-day fund yields, while SOFR is an overnight secured financing reference rate; the observed spreads are descriptive cross-measure comparisons rather than matched-horizon excess returns.
known_overclaims: Equating the gross-minus-net yield gap with a formally reported expense ratio.
Treating a same-date fund-yield-minus-SOFR spread as a matched-horizon excess return or guaranteed investor outcome.
